object_description: fully sunken library volume beneath an existing building
design_condition: The entire new volume is placed underground, with an entrance ramp and glazed atrium marking the intervention while creating a spacious but visually concealed relationship to the urban setting.

positive.statement: The enlarged public space and entrance gesture are surprising in their grandeur.

position.rationale: The pointed southern approach in plan marks the entrance gesture and adjoining public space.

positive.statement: The entrance situation is light-filled and spacious.

position.rationale: The entrance is constrained to the southern ramp edge, with elevated points indicating the upper access zone.

positive.statement: The public areas can be flexibly furnished and make optimal use of the atrium daylight.

position.rationale: The central elongated opening and surrounding volume identify the atrium-centered public zone.

positive.statement: The escape-route concept is well resolved.

position.rationale: Escape routes are not explicit; the marker follows the side access alignment within the sampled volume.

negative.statement: Hiding the entire additional volume underground suppresses the presence of the new institution and contributes little to the city’s urban development.

position.rationale: The point cloud shows a broad horizontal intervention with no above-ground mass, supporting the concealed-volume criticism.

negative.statement: The ramp appears empty at its full extent and gives the existing building an unjustifiably prominent position.

position.rationale: The ramp is approximated along the pointed southern approach visible in plan.

negative.statement: The access cores create an unattractive passage, poorly usable façade-side rooms, and undesirable blind zones.

position.rationale: Cores and side rooms are not separable; the marker uses the eastern perimeter band of the sampled volume.

negative.statement: Vertical access is inadequate, with a narrow staircase, hidden lifts, and no internal connections between key uses.

position.rationale: Vertical circulation is interior; the anchor is placed near the eastern access-side portion.

negative.statement: The underground construction, groundwater excavation, and relocation of the watercourse require great effort and lead to below-average sustainability.

position.rationale: The statement primarily evaluates construction effort, groundwater, and sustainability rather than a visible feature.
